## Incident Report — NetSupport RAT Infection (2024-11-26)

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 packets, 08:49:38–09:43:58 local/UTC+4), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt/.png` (Suricata alert export). Analysis performed with tshark.

### 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (`desktop-b8tqk49.nemotodes.health`) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES.HEALTH (DC: NEMOTODES-DC, 10.11.26.3) |
| Logged-in user account | **NEMOTODES\oboomwald** |

Confirmed via NBNS (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>/<20>`, workgroup `NEMOTODES`), LLMNR/mDNS (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49.local`), and Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic where `kerberos.CNameString = oboomwald`, realm `NEMOTODES.HEALTH`.

### 2. Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** — the commercial NetSupport Manager remote-access client, abused as a trojan/RAT.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, on two independent grounds:
1. Suricata/ET rule hits: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
2. Direct protocol/string confirmation in the pcap itself: HTTP POSTs to the C2 carry the literal `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` and cleartext NetSupport client protocol bodies (`CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1`, `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<encrypted blob>`) sent to `/fakeurl.htm` — this is the client's native check-in/command format, not an inference from behavior alone.

### 3. Timeline / infection chain

- **08:50:11–08:50:40** — Victim browses through an ad-redirect chain: `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) → `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207) → lands on `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), flagged by Suricata as a **ZPHP domain** (DNS lookup and TLS SNI). Several multi-megabyte TLS sessions to 193.42.38.139 follow (up to ~5.7 MB in one 5-second session) — consistent with a payload/installer fetch, though the transfer itself is encrypted so no filename/hash is recoverable from this capture.
- **08:50:45** — Newly-installed NetSupport client performs a geolocation lookup: `GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231), server returns `33.7488,-84.3877` (Atlanta, GA area) — legitimate NetSupport infrastructure used by the RAT to fingerprint the victim.
- **08:50:45 onward** — First C2 check-in to **194.180.191.64:443**, then continuous beaconing at ~60-second intervals (POST `/fakeurl.htm`) through **09:43:29**, i.e. still active when the capture ends (~53 minutes of C2 activity, ~90 check-ins).
- Note: `MS-EFSR EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` and SMBv1 events against the DC (10.11.26.3) occur at **08:49:55**, *before* the malicious redirect chain begins (08:50:11) — this is pre-existing domain/offline-files background traffic, unrelated to the compromise, and should not be attributed to the malware.

### 4. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2 (plaintext application protocol sent over TCP/443, no actual TLS handshake performed — port-443 camouflage). Endpoint: `POST /fakeurl.htm`, User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`.

**Malicious / suspicious domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 — delivery/lure site (Suricata: ZPHP domain in DNS lookup and TLS SNI)
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5 — redirect chain
- `confirmsubscription.com` → 52.8.34.0, 13.56.30.207 — redirect chain, returned tracking token `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` pointing to a further redirect host, 79.124.78.197

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`
- `https://modandcrackedapk.com/` (SNI-only visibility; payload delivery, encrypted)

**Legitimate-but-abused infrastructure**
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) `/location/loca.asp` — NetSupport's own geolocation service, queried by the malicious client post-install

**Files / hashes**
- No cleartext executable, installer, or archive transfer was observed in this capture — all payload-sized transfers occurred inside opaque TLS sessions. **No file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in the available traffic.**

### 5. Summary

DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user NEMOTODES\oboomwald, was compromised with NetSupport RAT after browsing through an ad-redirect chain (classicgrand.com → confirmsubscription.com) to a fake cracked-software lure site (modandcrackedapk.com, 193.42.38.139). The client immediately performed a NetSupport geolocation check-in and began sustained C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443, active for the duration of the capture. No lateral movement or file exfiltration was observed in this pcap.
